name: Saturn IB
tagline: Lifted Apollo 7, Skylab crews, and ASTP
dispatch: Not every Apollo job needed the Moon rocket. The Saturn IB was the pragmatic option — a crew-rated lifter for the work that stayed in Earth orbit: Apollo 7's shakedown of the redesigned spacecraft, the ferry flights to Skylab, and the handshake-in-orbit of Apollo-Soyuz. Its first stage was famously a bundle of tanks borrowed from the earlier Redstone and Jupiter missiles, clustered together — proven parts doing a new job rather than a clean-sheet design. It's the least glamorous rocket in the program, and a quiet lesson in not overbuilding: match the machine to the mission.
description: Saturn IB is a orbital launcher built by Chrysler / Douglas / IBM in USA. Lifted Apollo 7, Skylab crews, and ASTP. Retired after first flight in 1966.
